newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ'S BOLGER APOLOGISES TO FORMER SFO, TAX HEADS.
newsitem.headline: NZ'S BOLGER APOLOGISES TO FORMER SFO, TAX HEADS.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Thursday offered an apology to the former head of the Serious Fraud Office, Charles Sturt, and former Inland Revenue commissioner, David Henry after the "Winebox" inquiry cleared them of any wrongdoing.

"I am delighted that the commissioner's report clears them of any wrongdoing. I am very happy to apologise for any inconvenience or any embarrassment they suffered," Bolger said during question time in parliament.
Bolger was speaking after the publication of the conclusions of an inquiry launched nearly three years ago following revelations by current Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters.

The panel assessed a series of tax deals during the late 1980s involving the Cook Islands, a South Pacific territory which has so-called free association with New Zealand, and sought to substantiate allegations of fraud and malpractice levelled by Peters.

Commissioner Sir Ronald Davison concluded that neither the IRD nor the SFO had acted incompetently and, overall, he said "there is simply no evidence at all of the existence of such a fraud as he alleged in any of the winebox transactions".
The report is set to be used by opposition politicians to attack the credibility of Peters and the government.
ACT New Zealand MP Rodney Hide asked if Bolger would offer an "immediate and unreserved apology to Mr Sturt and Mr Henry for the hell that Mr Peters has put these two men through".
